chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: John T. Gibson's Standard Theater in Philadelphia
summary: Gibson owned the colored theatre where Jack Johnson and many comedians played; Sam Stiefel's Pearl was the rival.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Can you tell me a little bit about John T. Gibson?
Oh, he was the owner of a theater in Philadelphia. He'd been there for years. All different acts had been playing there for the longest -- even Jack Johnson played there.
He must have been seeing a lot of pretty good acts --

Oh, yeah, yeah, uh-huh. We had quite a lot of comedians, like Sandy Burns, Sam Russell, George Wilkshire, God rest their souls. He had plenty of entertainment coming in that theater. Then he had opposition -- Sam Stiefel had the Pearl Theater over on the other side of Philadelphia that booked a lot of colored acts, too.
